body.html: Leelawadee Resort Kham Muang sits in Tambon Thung Khlong, Kham Muang district, Kalasin province — about 2.6 km from the Kham Muang district office. It's a small bungalow resort of around 10 units that self-drivers passing through on errands, visitors coming to see Praewa silk weaving at Ban Phon, or travellers stopping overnight choose because it's easy to find and easy on the budget. Rooms are in separate bungalows with air-con, TV, a fridge, a desk, drinking water and an en-suite bathroom, plus free Wi-Fi and parking for self-drivers.

What guests praise most is clean rooms and a friendly owner. The reviews there note rooms that are clean for the price, with sockets and fittings working normally and a comfortable enough sleep for a night. The grounds are leafy and quiet in that out-of-town way, with no noise to speak of. For anyone who just needs a clean place to crash in Kham Muang — where rooms are harder to find than in the main town — this does the job at a wallet-friendly price.

"A cheap stay, conditions match the price — clean room, a comfortable sleep, sockets all working, and a friendly owner. Good for getting business done in the district. Just be ready for the rooms not to be new."

Another thing self-drivers rate is the handy base for exploring Praewa silk country. Kham Muang is the home of Ban Phon Praewa silk — the distinctive hand-woven cloth that's one of Kalasin's, and Thailand's, most prized. Staying here, you can drive out to the Ban Phon silk-weaving village to watch the weaving and shop for cloth with ease. With parking on site, it slots neatly into a road trip along Isan's cultural routes.

Now the honest part — this is a budget stay where the rooms aren't new and amenities cover only the essentials. Reviews say rooms are clean but plain, not modern, and some fittings are starting to show their age. As a small district resort, it doesn't have city-hotel facilities like a pool or gym. Online reviews are still few, so the score reflects a small sample — it's worth calling the resort directly to check availability and rates before you travel.

In short, Leelawadee Resort Kham Muang suits self-drivers who want a cheap base and need to spend a night in Kham Muang for business or to explore Praewa silk country. The score of around 7.1, from a small number of reviews, reflects it fairly — clean rooms, a friendly owner and good value, but rooms that aren't new and basic facilities. Set your expectations to the price and the purpose of your trip, and most travellers sleep fine for a night.

faqTitle: Frequently asked questions — Leelawadee Resort Kham Muang

faq.q: Where is Leelawadee Resort Kham Muang in Kalasin?
faq.a: It's in Tambon Thung Khlong, Kham Muang district, Kalasin province, about 2.6 km from the Kham Muang district office. Kham Muang is the home of Ban Phon Praewa silk and sits about 70 km from Kalasin town, so it's best for self-drivers.

faq.q: What are the starting prices and room types?
faq.a: Rooms start at around ฿400/night for a single, with a twin/double around ฿450 and possibly a version with breakfast. It's a small bungalow resort of around 10 units, and prices vary by season — it's best to call the resort directly to check availability and rates before you travel.

They're separate bungalow rooms, clean for the price, with air-con, TV, a fridge, a desk, drinking water and an en-suite bathroom. Reviews say rooms are clean and comfortable for a night with working sockets, but the rooms aren't new and are plainly furnished, so set your expectations to the price.
Yes — free Wi-Fi and parking on site, with quiet, leafy grounds in that out-of-town way. As a small resort, there's no pool or gym. For breakfast, it's best to confirm with the resort directly.

The highlight is the Ban Phon Praewa silk-weaving village in Kham Muang — an easy drive out to watch the weaving and shop for Kalasin's distinctive hand-woven cloth. With more time, the Sirindhorn (Dinosaur) Museum in Sahatsakhan and Lam Pao Dam are each about an hour's drive away.

faq.q: Who is this hotel best for?
faq.a: It's best for self-drivers who want a cheap base and need to overnight in Kham Muang for business or to explore Praewa silk country. It's less suited to anyone who needs a fresh property with full city-hotel facilities.
